chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said:
Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Wonder at the arrogant, the proud one, who was yesterday a drop of fluid, then tomorrow he will be a carcass.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on human pride and mortality?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on *tadhakkur* (remembrance of death) as a remedy for *kibr* (arrogance), contrasting the humble origin (*nutfah*) with the inevitable decay (*jifah*). It serves as a spiritual corrective for those who forget their mortality, a theme deeply rooted in the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding humility before God.
